abstract: We studied 40 consecutive patients with advanced germ-cell carcinoma and elevated serum levels of human chorionic gonadotropin (HCG) to assess the prognostic value of the magnitude of the decline in HCG levels after chemotherapy. If serum levels failed to become normal after the first chemotherapy cycle and if the day-22 HCG level/day-1 level was greater than 1/200 (0.005), an incomplete response to chemotherapy could be predicted with a sensitivity of 90% and a predictive value of 94%. Conversely, if the day-22 level was within normal limits, or if the day-22 level/day-1 level was less than 1/200, a successful response to chemotherapy (defined as a 1-year disease-free interval following cessation of chemotherapy) could be predicted with a sensitivity of 95% and a predictive value of 91% after one chemotherapy cycle. Overall, the long-term response to chemotherapy was correctly predicted in 37 of 40 patients (p less than 0.0001, compared with actual patient outcome using the chi-squared test).
abstract_ja: 進行期胚細胞癌で血清ヒト絨毛性ゴナドトロピン(hCG)が高値の患者40例を連続して検討し、化学療法後のhCG低下の程度がもつ予後的意義を評価した。第1回化学療法サイクル後も血清値が正常化せず、かつ第22日のhCG値/第1日値が1/200(0.005)を超える場合、不完全な奏効を感度90%、陽性的中率94%で予測できた。逆に、第22日の値が正常範囲内である場合、または第22日値/第1日値が1/200未満である場合は、1サイクル後の成功的奏効(化学療法終了後1年間の無病期間と定義)を感度95%、陽性的中率91%で予測できた。全体として、40例中37例で長期的な奏効を正しく予測した(p<0.0001、カイ二乗検定による実際の患者転帰との比較)。
